q: Compliance varies significantly by instruction category and by originating agent, indicating that adherence to ACF guidance is neither uniform nor automatic.
r: Include: empirical study of whether coding agents follow instructions in AGENTS.md-style context files (group b).

q: This paper studies whether a short value statement in an agent’s persistent instruction file changes not only how well the agent performs but also what it builds.
r: Include: effect of an instruction-file value statement on a coding agent's performance and output, with API cost logged (group b).

q: We evaluate Spark as a coach for AI coding agents performing software development tasks.
r: EC1: shared memory for coding agents, but evaluated only as single-snippet Python generation on DS-1000 judged by an LLM, with no agentic multi-step behaviour.

q: This paper presents the first large-scale empirical study to characterize this emerging form of developer-provided context.
r: Include: large-scale empirical study of Cursor rules files used with AI coding assistants (group b).

q: We introduce OctoBench to evaluate how models follow heterogeneous instructions in agentic coding tasks.
r: Include: benchmark of coding agents following repository policy files and skill documentation under three scaffolds (group b).

q: SWE-ContextBench complements existing coding and memory benchmarks by providing a realistic and controlled testbed for studying how agents retrieve, represent, and reuse prior contexts in software engineering tasks.
r: Include: benchmark of context and memory reuse in coding agents with accuracy, runtime and token-cost metrics (group b, not narrowed by EC6).

q: Reusable skills let LLM agents package task-specific procedures, tool affordances, and execution guidance into modular building blocks.
r: IC1: contribution is a retrieval and reranking model for skill routing at 80K-skill scale, not coding agents or their context files; coding agents appear only in a supplementary downstream check.

q: Each historical pull request is transformed into a natural-language task through an LLM-assisted prompt-generation pipeline, and the benchmark is formalized as a matched A/B comparison
r: EC6: benchmark protocol whose baseline measures repository-level file prediction from PR-derived prompts, not code development by an agent.

q: LLM-based coding agents rely on skills, prepackaged instruction sets that extend agent capabilities, yet every token of skill content injected into the context window incurs both monetary cost and attention dilution.
r: Include: study and token-reduction method for agent skills used by coding agents, measuring cost and functional quality (group b).

q: Agent skills are increasingly used to configure coding agents for software engineering (SE) tasks, yet current practice treats them as static, hand-crafted assets, or evolved on pass rate alone.
r: Include: skill bundles for coding agents on 16 SE tasks, 10 runs each, pass rate and inference cost (group b).
